svg.title: PATH: where the shell looks for commands.
svg.desc: PATH is a variable holding a colon-separated search list for command names without a slash. An illustrative lookup finds no ls in /usr/local/bin, finds it in /usr/bin and stops without searching /bin. In Bash, command -v ls reports what the shell would use; /usr/bin/ls is illustrative output when ls resolves to that executable rather than an alias or function. Using /usr/bin/ls names the illustrated program directly, bypassing PATH. The current directory is not automatically searched. Exporting PATH passes the list to child programs.
svg.text: PATH is a variable: directories searched for names without /.
Directories are separated by :. Search goes in order, stopping at the first usable match.
Illustrative lookup of ls. Example value, not a command:
In Bash, ask what the shell would use:
Shell-defined commands can take priority over PATH; your result may differ.
Here, ls searches; /usr/bin/ls directly names the illustrated program.
A slash bypasses search. ./ means here; the current directory is not automatically searched.
Exporting PATH passes the list to child programs, like other environment values.
